jei.sinkjourney.mechanical_lab.info: The stage-two bench: turns research notes from the primitive table into computation data and engraves the Steam blueprint. A hollow 3x3x3 brass shell with four upgrade slots.
jei.sinkjourney.trace_nexus.info: Engraves blueprints: feed blank blueprints, computation data and era materials, then spend FE. Upgrade modules can be installed on all four sides; the level slot decides which era can be engraved.
jei.sinkjourney.trace_compute.info: The CPU of the array: continuously consumes research substrate and water while venting steam. That steam must be reclaimed by the cooling core, otherwise backed-up outputs stall the computation.
jei.sinkjourney.trace_cooling.info: Continuously draws off the steam vented by the computation core and dissipates it as heat. It needs constant power; without it steam backs up and the CPU stops.
jei.kubejs.charcoal_furnace.info: A 3x3x3 brick-built charcoal furnace: crushed silver/gold and the electrum alloy can only be smelted here. Fuel is fed through the input bus; any coal or charcoal works (minecraft:coals).
jei.kubejs.charcoal_furnace.info2: Build layout: controller in the middle of the front face, input bus on its left, output bus on its right; a lit campfire sits at the very heart of the furnace (directly behind the controller) with a one-block flue left open at the top centre so you can see the flame. Dousing the fire halts the furnace; an atmospheric bellows attached anywhere to the furnace shell speeds it up by 20%.
jei.kubejs.charcoal_furnace.info3: Pyres cannot touch precious metals: crushed silver/gold have no pyre recipe at all; their reducing smelt belongs to the charcoal furnace only.
jei.kubejs.earth_blast_furnace.info: A 3x3x4 mud-brick earthen blast furnace: the dedicated iron reduction furnace. Crushed iron x2 + calcite x1 + coal/charcoal x2 -> iron ingot x2, 70s per batch. Vanilla smelting of iron ore, raw iron and iron dust has been removed.
jei.kubejs.earth_blast_furnace.info2: Build: set one electrum block into the middle of the bottom front row (the tuyere); the row above is input bus | controller | output bus, everything else is mud bricks; a lit campfire sits at the heart (directly behind the controller), and the two-block flue above it must reach the sky.
jei.kubejs.earth_blast_furnace.info3: Forced draft: an atmospheric bellows must be attached to the lower half of the shell (at or below tuyere height), otherwise the machine will not start. Dousing the campfire also halts it.
jei.kubejs.earth_blast_furnace.info4: Why: under forced draft the coal burns to CO first, and CO reduces the iron oxides; the calcite decomposes into CaO, which fluxes the silica/alumina gangue into slag, protecting the lining and cutting iron loss. Puddling/forging is abstracted away, so the furnace taps usable iron ingots directly.
